# Egap.Spreadsheets: guide for coding agents

Egap.Spreadsheets builds and edits workbooks from code and reads and writes Excel files (XLSX, XLSM, XLTX, XLTM) with
what they hold kept; it also reads and writes ODS and CSV, and reads XLSB and XLS. Sheets are sparse, up to 1,048,576 rows
by 16,384 columns. Formulas follow Excel's grammar and calculate through a dependency graph; tables, validation,
conditional formats, pivot tables, charts and printing to PDF are in the model.

Namespace: `Egap.Spreadsheets`, with `Egap.Documents.Charts` for charts and `Egami` and `Egami.Pixels` for rendered pages.

## Egap's vocabulary

Egap has its own names. Use them, not names from other PDF, Word or Excel libraries: there is no `PdfReader`, `PdfWriter`,
`XWPFDocument`, `Range.Text` or `IWorkbook` in Egap.

- `PdfDocument` (namespace `Egap.Pdf`) is a PDF file: `PdfDocument.Open`, `PdfDocument.Create`, `PdfDocument.Merge`, then
  `Pages`, `Metadata`, `Outline`, `Form`, `Attachments`, `Signatures` and `Save`. It is `IDisposable` and keeps its file open
  until disposed.
- `Document` (namespace `Egap.Documents`) is a flow document: one model for DOCX, DOC, RTF, ODT, plain text, PDF, HTML,
  MHTML, EPUB and Markdown. `Document.Load` and `Save` pick the format; `DocumentBuilder` edits at a cursor. It is not
  disposable.
- `Workbook` and `Worksheet` (namespace `Egap.Spreadsheets`) are an Excel workbook and its sheets; `sheet["B2"]` is a
  `Cell`, `sheet.Range("A1:C9")` a `CellRange`, and `CellValue` a cell's value.
- `Presentation` (namespace `Egap.Presentations`) is a PowerPoint file: `Presentation.Load`, `Slides`, `SlideMasters` and
  `Save`; `slide.Shapes` holds its `SlideShape`s.
- Each format has its own class (`DocxFormat`, `RtfFormat`, `OdtFormat`, `TextFormat`, `HtmlFormat`, `EpubFormat`,
  `MarkdownFormat`) and members on `Document` that forward to it: `Document.LoadDocx`, `SaveAsDocx`, `ToHtml`,
  `SaveAsMarkdown`. `SaveAsPdf` and `PdfConvert` (namespace `Egap.Documents.Pdf`) write PDF.
- Options are objects with `init` properties, set in an object initializer and passed to the call: `PdfReadOptions`,
  `PdfSaveOptions`, `PdfRenderOptions`, `PdfExportOptions`, `PdfConvertOptions`, `LayoutOptions`, `WorkbookLoadOptions`.
- Damaged input is repaired and reported, not thrown: `pdf.Warnings` (`PdfWarning`), a `Load` overload with
  `out IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning>`, and the list `Document.Save` returns. A `Strict` option throws instead.
- Sizes are PDF points (1/72 inch). `Length.Mm(15)`, `Length.Cm`, `Length.In` and `Length.Pt` (namespace `Egap.Pdf`) turn
  into points by themselves. Page indexes in code count from 0; `PdfPageRange.Parse("1-3,z")` takes page numbers from 1.
- Images, fonts and drawing come from Egami: a page renders to an Egami `Raster<Rgba8>` (namespaces `Egami` and
  `Egami.Pixels`), and draws onto any Egami.Drawing `Canvas`.
- Egap never opens a network connection by itself: the resolver, base folder or `HttpClient` you pass decides what a
  document may fetch.

## Entry points

- `Workbook.Create()` (one sheet, `Sheet1`), `Workbook.CreateEmpty()`, `Workbook.Load(path | stream,
  WorkbookLoadOptions)` and `Workbook.LoadCsv(path, CsvOptions)`. `WorkbookLoadOptions.Password` opens an encrypted file.
- `book.Save(path | stream, WorkbookSaveOptions)`: the extension picks the format, or `Format = WorkbookFormat.Xltx`
  names it; `Password` encrypts.
- `book.Worksheets` (`Add`, `Insert`, `Remove`, `Move`, `["Sales"]`, `[0]`), `book.Names`, `book.Calculate()`,
  `book.CalculateFull()`, `book.SaveAsPdf(path)`.
- `sheet["B2"]` and `sheet[row, column]` (from 0) give a `Cell`: `Value` (a `CellValue`), `Formula` (no `=`),
  `FormulaR1C1`, `Text` (as Excel shows it), `NumberFormat`, `Style`, `ImportData`.
- `sheet.Range("A1:C9")` gives a `CellRange`: `SetValues`, `GetValues`, `UpdateStyle`, `SetStyle`, `Clear`,
  `ClearContents`, `CopyTo`, `MoveTo`, `Sort`, `AutoFitColumns`, `ToDataTable`, `ToList<T>`.
- `sheet.Evaluate(formula)`, `InsertRows`, `DeleteRows`, `InsertColumns`, `DeleteColumns`, `FindAll`, `Replace`,
  `Tables`, `DataValidations`, `ConditionalFormats`, `PivotTables`, `Drawings`, `Comments`, `Hyperlinks`, `Protection`,
  `PageSetup`, `Paginate()`, `SaveAsPdf`, `SaveAsCsv`.
- `CellStyle.Default with { Font = CellFont.Default with { Bold = true } }`, `CellFill.Solid`, `CellColor.FromRgb`:
  immutable styles changed with `with`.
- `SheetWriter.Create(path)` and `SheetReader.Open(path)`: rows streamed through XLSX and CSV in constant memory.
- `SpreadsheetFormat.Register()` lets `Document.Load` read XLSX and CSV as documents; `Workbook.FromTables(document | pdf)`
  puts a document's tables on sheets.

## Samples

Build a sheet:

```csharp
using Egap.Spreadsheets;

Workbook book = Workbook.Create();                   // one empty sheet, Sheet1
Worksheet sheet = book.Worksheets[0];
sheet.Name = "Sales";

sheet["A1"].Value = "Region";
sheet["B1"].Value = "Amount";
sheet["A2"].Value = "North";
sheet["B2"].Value = 1250.5;
sheet["A3"].Value = "South";
sheet["B3"].Value = 980;
sheet["B4"].Formula = "SUM(B2:B3)";

sheet.Range("A1:B1").UpdateStyle(s => s with { Font = s.Font with { Bold = true } });
sheet.Range("B2:B4").UpdateStyle(s => s with { NumberFormat = "#,##0.00" });
```

Load, change and save:

```csharp
using Egap.Spreadsheets;

Workbook book = Workbook.Load("sales.xlsx");
Worksheet sheet = book.Worksheets["Sales"];
sheet["C2"].Value = 1300;
book.Save("sales.xlsx");

using MemoryStream stream = new();
book.Save(stream, new WorkbookSaveOptions { Format = WorkbookFormat.Xltx });
```

Calculate:

```csharp
using Egap.Spreadsheets;

Workbook book = Workbook.Create();
Worksheet sheet = book.Worksheets[0];
sheet["A1"].Value = 2;
sheet["B1"].Formula = "A1*3";
sheet["C1"].Formula = "B1+1";
book.Calculate();                                    // B1 is 6, C1 is 7

sheet["A1"].Value = 5;
CalculationResult result = book.Calculate();         // only B1 and C1 again
long count = result.Calculated;                      // 2

sheet.Range("D1:D3").SetArrayFormula("A1*{1;2;3}");  // D1:D3 are 5, 10, 15 after Calculate
CellRange? array = sheet["D2"].ArrayRange;           // D1:D3
```

Print to PDF and images:

```csharp
using Egami;
using Egami.Pixels;
using Egap.Pdf;
using Egap.Spreadsheets;

Workbook book = Workbook.Create();
Worksheet sheet = book.Worksheets[0];
for (int row = 0; row < 200; row++)
{
    sheet[row, 0].Value = $"Item {row + 1}";
    sheet[row, 1].Value = row * 1.5;
}

sheet.PageSetup.PrintTitleRows = RangeAddress.Parse("1:1");
sheet.PageSetup.RowBreaks.Add(100);                  // row 101 starts a page
sheet.PageSetup.Footer = "&CPage &P of &N";

SheetPrintLayout layout = sheet.Paginate();
int pages = layout.Pages.Count;                      // 6 on Letter: rows 1-44, 45-87, 88-100, 101-143, ...
sheet.SaveAsPdf("items.pdf");
sheet.SaveAsPdf("items-a.pdf", new SheetPdfOptions { Conformance = PdfAConformance.PdfA2a, Language = "en-US" });
Raster<Rgba8> firstPage = layout.Pages[0].Render(150);
```

Millions of rows:

```csharp
using Egap.Spreadsheets;

using (SheetWriter writer = SheetWriter.Create("orders.xlsx"))      // .csv, .tsv and .tab write text
{
    writer.StartSheet("Orders");
    writer.SetColumnWidth(0, 14);
    writer.SetColumnFormat(1, "yyyy-mm-dd");
    writer.FreezeTopRows(1);
    writer.WriteRow(CellStyle.Default with { Font = CellFont.Default with { Bold = true } }, "Order", "Date", "Amount");
    for (int i = 0; i < 1_000_000; i++)
    {
        writer.WriteRow($"A-{i}", 45000 + i % 365, i * 0.25);
    }
}

using SheetReader reader = SheetReader.Open("orders.xlsx");
double total = 0;
while (reader.Read())
{
    if (reader.Row > 0 && reader[2].Kind == CellValueKind.Number)
    {
        total += reader[2].Number;
    }
}

Console.WriteLine($"{reader.SheetName}: {total} ({reader.GetText(1)} was the last date)");
```

## Common mistakes

- Reading a formula's result straight after setting it. A formula's value is empty until `book.Calculate()`;
  `sheet.Evaluate` gives a value without recalculating the workbook.
- Writing formulas as a user types them in a localized Excel. `Formula` takes Excel's stored form: English function names,
  commas between arguments, no leading `=` (one given is dropped). Bad grammar throws a `FormulaException` with its
  `Position`.
- Mixing addresses: `sheet[3, 1]` is row 4, column B (both from 0), the same cell as `sheet["B4"]`.
- Confusing `Value` and `Text`. Dates are numbers shown through a date number format; `cell.Text` is what Excel would
  show, `cell.Value` the stored number.
- Expecting XLS or XLSB to be written. They are read only and save as XLSX (or ODS).
- `Cell` clashes with Egap.Documents' table `Cell` in a file that has both `using Egap.Documents;` and
  `using Egap.Spreadsheets;`: qualify one, or keep them in separate files.
- Building a workbook for a huge export. Use `SheetWriter` and dispose it to finish the file; use `SheetReader` to read
  rows without loading the workbook. `SheetWriter` does not stream an encrypted file.
- Using a workbook from several threads at once: a workbook is not safe to change from more than one thread.
- Catching the wrong exceptions: a file past `WorkbookLoadOptions.Limits` throws a `DocumentLimitException`, a wrong
  password a `DocumentPasswordException`, and a file that is no workbook a `DocumentException`, all from
  `Egap.Documents`.
